properties.description: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind (2004), directed by Michel Gondry and written by Charlie Kaufman, is a drama-romance with speculative science fiction elements starring Jim Carrey and Kate Winslet, with Tom Wilkinson and Mark Ruffalo in supporting roles. The story follows a man who undergoes a medical procedure to erase memories of his ex and then fights to preserve moments of their relationship as they are deleted. Combining nonlinear, dreamlike sequences with raw emotional scenes, the film explores themes of memory, identity, regret, and the paradoxes of love. Its tone is melancholic and thought‑provoking, balancing surreal visual inventiveness with intimate character work.
properties.plot_summary: After their relationship collapses, a couple turn to an experimental clinic that can erase specific memories of a person from one’s mind. As the procedure progresses, the man relives their time together inside his own consciousness and begins to resist the deletions. His attempts to hide and preserve precious moments force him to confront the full complexity of their love, heartbreak, and the role of memory in identity. The film interweaves surreal, dreamlike sequences with intimate, emotionally raw scenes to explore whether erasing pain also erases what made life meaningful.
